affiliations.organization_name_as_found: 621st Quartermaster Depot Company in Camp Polk, Louisiana
affiliations.date_precision: Institutional biography states service began in January 1944 and that he transferred to OSS Morale Operations in May 1944.

affiliations.date_precision: The biography describes freelance writing and radio work before his July 1943 Army induction but does not provide exact start or end dates for every engagement.
affiliations.research_notes: Published as self-employment rather than inventing a single employer. The page also documents Refugee Artists Group membership and radio work but does not prove an employment relationship with WMCA.

affiliations.date_precision: The University of Chicago finding aid says he taught at Harvard through completion of his doctorate in 1942 and then went to wartime Washington positions beginning in 1943.
affiliations.research_notes: Harvard is the best-supported last civilian employer before his wartime Washington work. The finding aid groups OSS with several policy and planning commissions, so it does not prove which government assignment immediately preceded OSS.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Private First Class Lothar Metzl is confirmed as the Austrian writer transferred from the U.S. Army to OSS Morale Operations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name, rank, protected identifier, and Box 520 personnel-file reference all align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an institutional biography grounded in the named OSS personnel file and corroborated by the official Army bulk entry.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography supplies a month-by-month Army-to-OSS sequence in 1944.
claims.match_notes: The project page explicitly credits NARA RG 226, Entry 224, Box 520; protected identifier omitted from public data.

claims.claim_text: Lothar Metzl's immediate pre-OSS assignment was the U.S. Army's 621st Quartermaster Depot Company at Camp Polk.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In May of that year, he was transferred as an author for the Morale Operations Branch
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography places him with the 621st company from January 1944 and explicitly dates his transfer to OSS to May.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed identity from the personnel-file-grounded biography, exact index record, and Army entry.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence: January 1944 unit service followed by a May 1944 OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: Published as a military assignment, not as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Lothar Metzl's best-supported last civilian status before Army service was freelance writing and radio work in New York.
claims.evidence_excerpt: He worked as a free-lance playwright, satirist, and (cabaret) author
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The biography describes freelance authorship, Refugee Artists Group participation, and anti-fascist radio work before his July 1943 draft.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed identity from the personnel-file-grounded biography and exact protected-identifier match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before July 1943 Army induction; no single employing firm is established.
claims.match_notes: Recorded as self-employment; WMCA is not labeled an employer because the source documents participation rather than employment.

claims.claim_text: Indexed P-5 employee Lloyd A. Metzler is identified with high confidence as economist Lloyd Appleton Metzler.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name and middle initial align with an institutional finding aid that explicitly documents OSS work from 1943 to 1946.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare full name and an authoritative institutional source explicitly linking that person to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The finding aid places Harvard work through 1942 and wartime Washington service beginning in 1943.
claims.match_notes: Appleton is retained as a documented full-middle-name variant; Box 520 can provide direct personnel-file confirmation.

claims.claim_text: Harvard University is Lloyd A. Metzler's best-supported last civilian employer before his wartime Washington service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: He served as an instructor and tutor at Harvard and completed a Ph.D. in economics in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The finding aid says he taught at Harvard through 1942 and then went to Washington, where OSS and other wartime commissions employed him from 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the rare exact name and explicit OSS service in the institutional biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable last civilian employer; multiple government assignments in 1943-1946 prevent identifying the affiliation immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Harvard employment and student status are modeled separately; this claim concerns his documented instructor and tutor roles.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Technician Fifth Grade Walter J. Meuller has a high-confidence match to official Army Walter J. Mueller.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A nonshared protected identifier and compatible grade connect the two spellings.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the unique identifier, initials, rank context, and a transposition limited to the indexed surname spelling.
claims.temporal_assessment: Identity context only; Army codes do not establish a named predecessor employer.
claims.match_notes: Official bulk record ordinal 3715872. Both Meuller and Mueller remain visible; the protected identifier is omitted from public data.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Lieutenant Joshua M. Mewborn has a high-confidence match to a 502nd Parachute Infantry second lieutenant.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary order gives the same uncommon full name, officer grade, and protected officer identifier printed in the OSS index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from three specific agreeing identifiers beyond the surname alone.
claims.temporal_assessment: The order documents a November 1944 military assignment but does not establish when he entered OSS.
claims.match_notes: The 502nd assignment is identity context only and is not labeled immediate pre-OSS without a transfer chronology.
